title: Period, Symmetry, and Graph of s = -tan(pi*t)
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Graph the function s = -\tan(\pi t) in the ts-plane. Determine its fundamental period and state the symmetry of its graph.

steps.title: Compute the Fundamental Period
steps.explanation: The standard tangent function has fundamental period pi. Scaling the input by pi produces a fundamental period of pi/pi = 1.
steps.why: -tan(pi*(t + 1)) = -tan(pi*t + pi) = -tan(pi*t) by the pi-periodicity of tangent.

steps.title: Identify Asymptotes, Zeros, and Monotonicity
steps.explanation: On its principal branch (-1/2, 1/2), the curve passes through (0, 0) and decreases strictly from +infinity to -infinity because of the leading negative sign.
steps.why: cos(pi*t) = 0 when pi*t = pi/2 + k*pi, which simplifies to t = 1/2 + k.

steps.title: Test for Symmetry
steps.explanation: Since s(-t) = -s(t), the function is odd, and its graph is symmetric with respect to the origin.
steps.why: Negating an odd function preserves its odd parity.
